name: fastd
why: A tunnelling daemon with a mesh VPN lineage; a real door into tunnelling, though mostly plumbing.

brief.what_it_is: fastd is a very small VPN daemon that tunnels IP packets and Ethernet frames over UDP. It takes network packets or frames from a local interface, encrypts and authenticates them with one of several supported schemes, and sends them to peers over UDP. It can be set up in 1:1, 1:n, or meshed topologies. The README does not say much more about inputs and outputs.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit motivation. It presents fastd as a small, general-purpose tunnelling daemon that supports modern encryption and authentication and several network topologies.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism. The docs index lists a configuration file format, peer configuration, encryption and authentication method providers (ec25519, FHMQV-C, AES128-CTR, Salsa20, GHASH/GCM, UHASH/UMAC, Poly1305, and others), an MTU guide, and a protocol specification with a handshake format and payload packet description. I did not open those pages.
brief.install_notes: The README says binary packages are provided by many major Linux distributions and runs on Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and macOS. The docs index has pages on building fastd, dependencies, and build settings, which I did not read. I did not see first-run steps, configuration examples, or account requirements.
brief.standout: fastd is a small daemon with a broad set of pluggable encryption and authentication methods, and it supports 1:1, 1:n, and meshed layouts from one binary. The docs also contain a protocol specification and a fairly deep cryptography section, which is unusual for a tool this size.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the evidence is thin. The docs index lists release notes up to fastd v23 with no dates, and I did not see a last-commit date or a maintainer note. The README's note that Android support is unmaintained is the only explicit status statement.
brief.caveats: Android support is in the code but unmaintained, according to the README. I only read the README and the docs index page; the command-line options page returned 404 and the configuration, build, and protocol pages were not read. I found no commands in the sources I read, so no command lines are quoted. The scout note calls it mostly plumbing, and the README supports that reading.
quotes: fastd is a very small VPN daemon which tunnels IP packets and Ethernet frames over UDP.
It supports various modern encryption and authentication schemes and can be used in many different network topologies (1:1, 1:n, meshed).
Android support exists in the code, but is currently unmaintained.
